data.long_meaning: Siva (God) + Anand (Bliss, Auspicious, Graceful). The name Sivanand carries the meaning “Auspicious, Graceful, Auspicious One” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil. Parents who choose Sivanand usually hope their child will grow to embody auspicious, graceful, auspicious one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sivanand is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, paying homage to Lord Shiva, the Hindu deity of destruction and regeneration. The name is a reflection of the reverence and devotion towards Lord Shiva, thus instilling a sense of pride and identity within the Hindu community.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, Sivanand represents the divine union between the individual soul (atman) and the supreme soul (Brahman) or Lord Shiva, through the experience of eternal bliss or Anand. It is believed that chanting the name Sivanand can bring spiritual growth, emotional peace, and a deep sense of connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sivanand means "auspiciousness of Shiva." It symbolizes the inner awakening to the divine presence of Shiva within, fostering peace, wisdom, and bliss in one's life.

historical_references.reference: Sivaraman Swami Sivanand was born on September 8, 1887, in Pattamonur, Tamil Nadu, India. He renounced the world in 1924 and took the name Sivanand. He founded the Divine Life Society in 1932, which is headquartered at Rishikesh in the Himalayas.
historical_references.context: Founding of the Divine Life Society and taking the name Sivanand.

historical_references.reference: Sivanand was a prominent figure in the Hindu reform movement during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He was influenced by the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and Vivekananda. Sivanand wrote over 300 books on various aspects of Hinduism and spirituality, and his teachings continue to be popular among Hindus around the world.
historical_references.context: Hindu reform movement and influential spiritual teacher and writer.
